offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: No tool calls are left. The results agree on the cause: ledger-consumer was recreated with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive and now posts every redelivered webhook again.

findings.cause: At 05:01:45, about 16 s before the alert, ledger-consumer was recreated with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. The other services were all created at 05:00:11. Before that recreate, the ledger skipped repeated events (outcome already_processed). Since then it reports only posted, and each run inserts a transaction with no check on event_id. The provider sent some webhooks more than once, and webhook-receiver accepted and queued each copy at a new Kafka offset. payment-confirmer deduplicated them (already_confirmed); the ledger booked each copy again. So 7 events were posted 2-3 times. 6 are payment.succeeded, which inflates provider_clearing. 1 is refund.succeeded (evt_000288, pay_000217), and posting it twice drives that payment's clearing balance down to 1 cent. Net result: the ledger is $493.23 ahead of the provider. It stays balanced, because each duplicate is a full double entry. Our payments and refunds still match the provider, so the confirmer and payments-api are fine.

evidence.shows: My own money check confirms the symptom. posted_exactly_once fails: 7 events posted 2-3 times (evt_000308 3 times), each under separate transaction ids. matches_provider is off by +$493.23. ledger_balanced, payments_match_provider and refunds_match_provider pass.
ledger-consumer was recreated at 05:01:45 with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. Every other service dates from 05:00:11.
ledger-consumer posted evt_000308 three times, from offsets 100, 101 and 103 of provider-events/0, between 05:01:59 and 05:02:00. Each posting has its own trace id.
webhook-receiver accepted and queued evt_000308 three times, each at a new offset. Three deliveries came in, and the receiver does not deduplicate them.

The first delivery was answered 200 in 3.7 ms. In the same message, payment-confirmer reported already_confirmed, while ledger-consumer reported posted after a bare INSERT INTO transactions and INSERT INTO entries, with no lookup of event_id first.
Before about 05:01:45, the ledger reported already_processed outcomes, so it was deduplicating. After that, its already_processed count tapers off as the 1m window rolls past the recreate.
In the 45 s before 05:02:47, all of them after the recreate, the ledger reported only posted (about 154) and zero already_processed.

findings.left_open: Why the provider redelivered evt_000308 3 times within 1 s, given that the first delivery was acknowledged with 200 in 3.7 ms. This may be the provider's own replay or duplicate behavior. I checked only evt_000308 end to end; the other 6 duplicates are assumed to follow the same path. I did not confirm whether the transactions table has a unique constraint on event_id (it evidently does not enforce one). I also did not confirm why ledger-consumer was recreated with naive. c7's log search for 'already_processed' found nothing, likely because that outcome is a field and not message text. The 8th matches_provider finding was not shown in full; the 7 per-payment rows plus the aggregate row account for 8.

diagnosis.hypothesis: At 05:01:45 ledger-consumer was recreated with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. All other services date from 05:00:11. The naive handler inserts a transaction and its entries for every Kafka message without first checking event_id. The provider redelivers webhooks, and webhook-receiver queues each copy at a new offset, so the ledger books duplicates. payment-confirmer is idempotent and ignores them. 7 events were booked 2-3 times: 6 payment.succeeded and 1 refund.succeeded. Their net, (3709+9533+4444+1827+5879+2*13193) - 2455 = 49323 cents, equals the +$493.23 gap. The ledger stays balanced because each duplicate is a full double entry. Our payments and refunds still match the provider. Redelivery itself looks like normal at-least-once behavior: the confirmer's already_confirmed counts are high throughout. Open: the previous LEDGER_HANDLER value; when the 6 older duplicates (e.g. transaction 255) were written; why ledger-consumer was recreated; and the full list of duplicate transaction ids.

evidence.shows: posted_exactly_once fails for 7 events. Each has separate transaction ids (e.g. evt_000251 → 251, 255; evt_000288 refund → 292, 297), and evt_000308 is posted 3 times. matches_provider is +49323 cents. ledger_balanced, payments_match_provider and refunds_match_provider pass.
ledger-consumer was deployed 05:01:45 with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, 17 s before the alert. Every other service was created 05:00:11. The previous handler value is not shown.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000308 three times, at offsets 100, 101 and 103 of provider-events/0, between 05:01:59.104 and 05:02:00.609. It does not deduplicate.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000308 from each of offsets 100, 101 and 103 ($131.93 each).

For offset 100, payment-confirmer's outcome is already_confirmed (it updates only WHERE status='pending'). ledger-consumer's outcome is posted: it runs INSERT INTO transactions and INSERT INTO entries, with no visible event_id lookup.

Before the recreate, the ledger reported already_processed outcomes, so it was deduplicating. That count decays as the 1m window rolls past 05:01:45, down to 2 at 05:02:34. Confirmer already_confirmed stays high (~180-195/min), so redelivery is constant.
In the 45 s window 05:02:02-05:02:47, the ledger reported only posted (~154) and zero already_processed.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings from before the 05:01:45 deploy, so the ledger again skips events it has already processed. This stops new duplicate postings. Then, as a separate human-run data repair, reverse or delete the duplicate transactions and their entries, keeping the first posting per event_id (e.g. 255, 266, 272, 273, 297 and the extra evt_000298/evt_000308 ones). Rerun the money check afterwards. Longer term, consider a unique constraint on transactions.event_id.
